title: Unredacted operational screenshot is included in portable release packages

locations.symbol: binary artifact sentinel (not a source-line claim)

observed_behavior: The tracked PNG visibly contains the Windows user name lmmye, the internal host/share path \\LAYNE-SERVER\Users\Layne\Videos\outsource\Movies, a local AppData temporary-file path, process IDs, run IDs, and timestamps. The release exclusion policy returns included for this path, and binary assets are not eligible for the portable-package content scan.
expected_invariant: Portable release artifacts must exclude or redact repository evidence that discloses personal identifiers, private host/share topology, local filesystem paths, or transient operational identifiers.
root_cause: The release policy has no exclusion or redaction rule for ops/release/evidence binary screenshots, while the content-safety scan is text-file-only.
failure_scenario: A portable release is distributed and silently carries the screenshot, exposing an operator identity and internal infrastructure/path details to every recipient.
evidence: Visual inspection of the 1294x1399 RGBA PNG showed the user, host/share, local temporary path, PIDs, run IDs, and timestamps.
ops/scripts/release/build.ps1 copies every included file and hashes the copy-plan entry but performs no semantic inspection of included binary media.
The image is referenced as historical proof by ops/release/changes/unreleased/MP-CHANGE-2026-0704-002 and therefore has a legitimate evidence purpose, but the checked-in copy is unredacted.
existing_safeguards: Portable-package manifest records SHA-256 for copied files.
Text-eligible included files undergo a content scan.
safeguard_gap: Integrity hashing detects mutation, not disclosure, and the binary PNG bypasses the text content scan.
tests_present: Release-policy tests cover selected excluded directories and personal configuration.
tests_missing: An assertion that ops/release/evidence screenshots are excluded or explicitly redacted.
A binary-asset privacy review gate for portable-release inputs.
recommended_remediation: Replace the checked-in screenshot with a redacted evidence image or an equivalent text proof that removes personal and network identifiers, and exclude raw evidence screenshots from portable packages unless explicitly allowlisted. Add a release-policy regression test.
remediation_risk: low: redaction must preserve enough visible evidence to support the associated change packet
validation_rung: Run the focused release-policy tests, rebuild a portable package, inspect its manifest and payload, and visually verify the replacement evidence.
prior_audit_relationship: New binary-content and package-boundary finding from the exhaustive W13 inventory.

observed_behavior: Nine JPEG mobile-game screenshots under .codex-remote-attachments are tracked as ordinary Git blobs, total 1,488,782 bytes, have no product or documentation consumers, and are included by the default portable-release policy. The generated code-context service explicitly excludes this namespace as remote attachment material, but release tooling and .gitignore do not.
expected_invariant: Ephemeral user/assistant attachments that are unrelated to product behavior must not become durable repository or release payload without an explicit evidence purpose, owner, provenance decision, and package policy.
root_cause: The repository excludes .codex but has no equivalent ignore or release-exclusion rule for .codex-remote-attachments, so a broad checkpoint commit and broad release copy plan captured the files.
failure_scenario: Portable builds accumulate unrelated third-party screenshots and potentially account-state imagery, increasing package size and redistributing material that was supplied only as transient assistant context.
evidence: All nine files are JPEG 597x1280 RGB images with no EXIF and were individually visually inspected as Uma Musume mobile-game roster/card/selection screens.
Bounded reference searches found no active consumer for any attachment path or filename.
All nine were introduced together by commit 039658158d8439a868eff3c8c37e314845e9e22a (Update media pipeline architecture and tooling).
Get-MediaPipelineReleaseExclusionReason returned <included> for every file; binary content-scan eligibility was false.
src/mediapipeline/tools/dev/code_context_service.py excludes .codex-remote-attachments from code context, demonstrating that the namespace is attachment input rather than product source.
existing_safeguards: The code-context service ignores remote attachments.
Release manifests hash files that are copied.
safeguard_gap: Neither safeguard prevents tracking or packaging, and no license/privacy review is required before broad binary copying.
tests_present: Release-policy tests assert exclusion of the .codex directory.
tests_missing: A portable-release policy assertion that remote attachments are absent.
recommended_remediation: Remove the nine unrelated attachments from the active tree, ignore the attachment namespace, exclude it in release policy, and add regression tests. Preserve only deliberately selected and documented evidence outside the ephemeral namespace.
remediation_risk: low: first verify no current audit or operator workflow intentionally depends on the screenshots
validation_rung: Run release-policy tests, build and inspect a portable package, and run bounded repository-reference checks for the removed paths.
prior_audit_relationship: New repository and packaging hygiene finding from the exhaustive W13 binary inventory.

title: Substantial Refactoring UI text is Git-distributed without repository redistribution provenance

locations.symbol: binary artifact sentinel (not a source-line claim)

observed_behavior: The tracked DOCX contains 15,723 words across 41 rendered pages and eight major sections attributed in the document to Adam Wathan and Steve Schoger. Core properties say it is a text-only conversion from a user-provided PDF and name Layne Myers as creator/last modifier. The repository contains no LICENSE, NOTICE, permission record, or source citation establishing redistribution rights. The official Refactoring UI site describes the work as a paid Tailwind Labs book and provides only limited free material. The DOCX is excluded from the portable release but remains distributed through Git.
expected_invariant: A repository-distributed substantial copy or conversion of third-party paid publication content must have documented source and redistribution authorization, or be replaced by a lawful reference or independently authored notes.
root_cause: The Office working-document exclusion addresses portable packaging but change intake has no provenance/license gate for binary documents committed to Git.
failure_scenario: Repository clones, mirrors, or source archives redistribute a substantial third-party text without evidence that the project is entitled to do so, creating avoidable copyright and supply-chain provenance exposure.
evidence: Structural inspection: 886 paragraphs (885 nonempty), 15,723 words, 88,125 characters, eight Heading 1 sections, no tables or images, and no external relationships, macros, comments, or tracked revisions.
Word 16 exported the DOCX read-only to a 41-page PDF; every rendered page was visually inspected and contained coherent book text without clipping or hidden-image substitution.
Core properties: title Refactoring UI - Text Only; description Text-only conversion from user-provided PDF; creator/lastModifiedBy Layne Myers; created/modified 2026-05-17.
https://refactoringui.com/ identifies Refactoring UI by Adam Wathan and Steve Schoger as a paid book from Tailwind Labs with only limited free chapters.
Bounded reference search found no active inbound consumer; docs/generated/DOC_ARCHIVE_CANDIDATE_SCAN.md records zero active inbound references.
Release policy excludes the DOCX as a local Office working document, but Git tracks it as an ordinary blob.
affected_flows: Git clone and source archive distribution
existing_safeguards: Portable release policy excludes local Office working documents.
The generated archive-candidate scan identifies zero active inbound references.
safeguard_gap: Neither safeguard documents redistribution entitlement or prevents Git/source-archive distribution.
tests_present: Portable-release policy recognizes Office working documents.
tests_missing: Repository intake/license gate for substantial third-party binary documents.
A provenance record linking this conversion to an authorized distributable source.
recommended_remediation: Until redistribution rights are documented, remove the DOCX from the tracked active repository and replace it with a lawful link plus independently authored project-specific notes if needed. If permission exists, record the source, license/permission scope, attribution, and intended distribution boundary.
remediation_risk: medium: retain any genuinely project-specific annotations separately before removal and avoid asserting infringement without a rights review
validation_rung: License/provenance review, bounded inbound-reference scan, Git/source-package inventory check, and portable-release policy regression.
prior_audit_relationship: New third-party provenance finding from W13 structural, visual, and packaging inspection; this records unresolved entitlement rather than a legal conclusion.
